node.title: Re: Is it possible to get all variable names which are declared? (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
The fact that you want to do this means that you are either writing a debugger, or you are looking at the problem from the wrong angle (e.g. [https://perl.plover.com/varvarname.html|"it's stupid to use a variable as a variable name"], and you should use a hash instead). If you could tell us why you want to do this, we can almost certainly provide better solutions.

[mod://PadWalker] will provide you with enough rope to shoot yourself in the foot:

use warnings; use strict; use PadWalker qw/peek_my/; use Data::Dump; my $A; my $B = 0; dd peek_my(0); for my $i ( $B .. 3 ){ my $C = 3; dd peek_my(0); } __END__ { "\$A" => \undef, "\$B" => \0 } { "\$A" => \undef, "\$B" => \0, "\$C" => \3, "\$i" => \0 } { "\$A" => \undef, "\$B" => \0, "\$C" => \3, "\$i" => \1 } { "\$A" => \undef, "\$B" => \0, "\$C" => \3, "\$i" => \2 } { "\$A" => \undef, "\$B" => \0, "\$C" => \3, "\$i" => \3 }

Update: That only dumps my variables. See also the module's peek_our function, or for inspecting the [doc://perlmod#Symbol-Tables] of packages, [mod://Devel::Symdump] or my simplistic replacement [https://github.com/haukex/Config-Perl/blob/d5b2b68052ce8ff8d77f392014c3ff6ef6f7f3ba/t/Config_Perl_Testlib.pm#L103|here] (only does scalars, arrays and hashes). When dumping symbol tables, note the caveat described in the [mod://Devel::Symdump] documentation: "scalar symbol table entries are a special case. If a symbol table entry exists at all, presence of a scalar is currently unknowable, due to a feature of Perl described in [doc://perlref#Making-References|"Making References" in perlref] point 7. For example, this package will mark a scalar value $foo as present if any of @foo, %foo, &foo etc. have been declared or used."
